title: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

relationships.phenotype: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene (615712) on chromosome 5p15.2.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
checks.explanation: The paper reports heterozygous OTULIN mutation causing ORAS-like disease; AIPDSA is the OMIM name for it.

checks.claim: The OTULIN gene is located on chromosome 5p15.2.
checks.evidence_quote: we identify two patients with the heterozygous mutation p.Cys129Ser in OTULIN
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that the paper does not state.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is an autoinflammatory disorder that begins in infancy. Features include recurrent panniculitis, pathergy with sterile pustular abscesses, sterile necrotizing inflammation of skin and soft tissues, poor wound healing, fever, and edema. Laboratory findings include markedly raised C-reactive protein (CRP) and neutrophilia. Davidson et al. (2024) described the disorder as resembling OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS), which is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants, but the autosomal dominant form results from a heterozygous dominant negative variant.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) described a 22-month-old Caucasian boy (P1) whose parents were not consanguineous. He was born at 31 weeks' gestation. At 4 days of age he developed peri-umbilical erythema with sterile neutrophilic inflammation around a urachal remnant. After surgery the wound dehisced and did not close, and he later developed a spontaneous cutaneous duodenal stoma. At 8 weeks of age he had an acute respiratory deterioration with body edema, hypotension, and presumed pulmonary edema, which responded to corticosteroids. He had recurrent panniculitis and pathergy, with sterile pustular abscesses at injection and cannula sites. An echogenic focus on the tricuspid valve was treated as culture-negative endocarditis. Laboratory findings included raised CRP (100-200 mg/L), neutrophilia, monocytosis, eosinophilia, persistent thrombocytopenia, and initial hypogammaglobulinemia. A skin biopsy showed acute inflammatory exudate with suppuration and necrosis.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) also described a Saudi girl (P2) born at term to nonconsanguineous parents. At 7 months of age, 2 weeks after routine vaccinations, she presented with fever, generalized edema, and multiple tender skin lesions. The lesions progressed to cellulitis-like plaques and necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration, which required debridement and fasciotomy. She had leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and a high CRP (264 mg/L). All cultures were negative, and a biopsy showed infiltration by neutrophils and plasma cells, with necrosis. At 12 months of age she had a second attack with fever, erythematous plaques, and a CRP of 393 mg/L. A skin biopsy at that time showed panniculitis. She responded promptly to corticosteroids.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) found markedly increased transcription of IFNB1 and IL6, and to a lesser extent TNF, in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from P1. Fibroblasts from P1 had an elevated interferon-stimulated gene score. The score was similar to that of fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS and higher than that of fibroblasts from healthy donors or OTULIN-haploinsufficient individuals. THP-1 monocytes stably expressing C129S OTULIN showed a similar inflammatory gene signature, whereas cells expressing wildtype OTULIN did not.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) characterized the C129S mutant functionally. Its thermostability was similar to that of wildtype OTULIN, and levels of OTULIN and of the LUBAC components were normal in patient fibroblasts. However, the mutant could not hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin. An activity-based probe showed that active wildtype OTULIN and inactive C129S OTULIN were coexpressed in roughly equal amounts in patient fibroblasts. Surface plasmon resonance showed that C129S OTULIN bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity. M1-linked ubiquitin chains accumulated in patient fibroblasts. In HEK293T cells, which express endogenous OTULIN, transfection of C129S OTULIN caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation. Wildtype OTULIN and the loss-of-function variants Y244C and N341D did not have these effects. C129S OTULIN still drove NF-kappa-B activity when cotransfected with wildtype OTULIN at lower ratios, indicating a dominant negative effect.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) found that fibroblasts from patients with the C129S mutation were as sensitive to cell death induced by TNF plus cycloheximide as fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS. They were more sensitive than fibroblasts from OTULIN-haploinsufficient individuals or healthy donors. The cell death was mainly apoptotic: caspase inhibition reduced it, whereas necrostatin-1 had little effect. TNF-induced MAPK and NF-kappa-B signaling and IL-6 and IL-8 secretion were largely normal in patient fibroblasts.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that C129S OTULIN binds LUBAC. In cells, the mutant promoted ubiquitination of the LUBAC component SHARPIN and, to a lesser extent, HOIP. Patient fibroblasts showed increased interaction between OTULIN and LUBAC, and most of the LUBAC-bound OTULIN was catalytically inactive. In patient cells, recruitment of LUBAC components (HOIP and SHARPIN) to the TNFR1 signaling complex was reduced, as was RIPK1 modification. The authors concluded that M1-ubiquitin accumulating on LUBAC reduces its recruitment to TNFR1 and promotes TNF-induced cell death, leading to necrotizing tissue.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) reported that both of their patients responded to corticosteroids. In P1, adalimumab allowed the steroid dose to be reduced, lowered CRP, and supported wound healing. Ruxolitinib was also tried in P1, but its benefit was unclear. P2 was treated with infliximab plus methotrexate, was weaned off steroids, and remained in remission for 2 years. Prophylactic antibiotics improved wound healing in P1 and controlled recurrent chest infections in P2.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) reported 2 unrelated children with AIPDSA who carried a de novo heterozygous cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution in the catalytic domain of OTULIN, caused by 2 different nucleotide changes. In P1, a Caucasian boy, trio exome sequencing identified a c.386G-C transversion, which was not present in gnomAD. In P2, a Saudi girl, whole-genome sequencing identified a c.385T-A transversion, and testing of the parents confirmed that it was de novo.

checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
checks.explanation: The variant was de novo in both patients.

checks.claim: OTULIN C129 lies in the catalytic domain.
checks.evidence_quote: Significantly, cysteine 129 is part of the OTULIN catalytic domain

checks.claim: The OTULIN C129S substitution in the 2 AIPDSA patients was caused by 2 different nucleotide changes.
checks.evidence_quote: ENST00000284274.5:c.385T>A, which results in the same cysteine to serine change at position 129

checks.claim: In P1, a Caucasian boy with AIPDSA, trio exome sequencing identified an OTULIN c.386G-C transversion.
checks.evidence_quote: Trio exome sequencing was performed on P1 and his parents; this identified a de novo variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.386G>C

checks.evidence_quote: absent from databases of normal variation, including gnomAD (v2.1.1 and v3.1.2)

checks.evidence_quote: P2 underwent whole genome sequencing and a variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.385T>A

checks.claim: Parental testing confirmed that the OTULIN c.385T-A transversion in P2 was de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: Follow-up testing on P2’s parents confirmed the de novo nature of the variant

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that the C129S mutant was thermostable but could not hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin, and that it bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity. Patient fibroblasts expressed roughly equal amounts of active wildtype and inactive mutant OTULIN, and M1-linked ubiquitin chains accumulated in these cells. In HEK293T cells, C129S OTULIN caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation, even when cotransfected with wildtype OTULIN at lower ratios, indicating a dominant negative effect.
